lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: The Tiny Hour! A programme for very small listeners. Please lean in.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Hello, small ones! It's The Tiny Hour, from inside a matchbox.

lines.speaker: Dot, the Ladybird
lines.text: This is The Tiny Hour!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Well done, Dot!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: The Tiny Hour, on one hundred and four point three five. That's a big number. We're very proud of it.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Good morning, small ones! It's breakfast time! I've got one oat. You've got one oat. Let's chew!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Breakfast tip! One grain of sugar is enough for six of us. Give it a lick, and pass it on.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Sharing is caring! And a bit sticky!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: It's Crafternoon! Gather round the matchbox, everyone. Mind the pencil. It's rolling.

lines.speaker: Dot, the Ladybird
lines.text: Auntie Pim, what's that big round thing?

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: That's a button, Dot! We could make a table out of it! Or a trampoline! Or a very small moon!

lines.speaker: Dot, the Ladybird
lines.text: Can it be all three?

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: On Crafternoon, everything can be all three!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Hello, small ones. It's the very small hours. The big people are asleep. Let's be very quiet.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: If you can't sleep, listen to the big clock. Every tick is the clock saying: still here. Still here. It's a very good clock.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: And hello to the operator on the big ship out there. From far enough away, you're quite small too. You're very welcome here.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Here's the goodnight song. Whisper it with me.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: The moon is a button, the stars are pins,

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: the night is a blanket, so tuck yourself in.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: The big clock ticks, and the big house sleeps.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Goodnight, small ones. And not a peep.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Crafty Corner! Today we're making a hat out of a raindrop. You'll need one raindrop, and somewhere dry to put it.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Crafty Corner! Today, a bed made from a matchbox. I'm sitting on mine! You'll need a matchbox, and something soft. A dandelion clock is perfect.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Crafty Corner! A sail for your boat, from one sweet wrapper. Ask a grown-up for a sweet. Eat the sweet. Keep the wrapper.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: It's Crafty Corner! Today: a lovely warm scarf, knitted from one strand of wool. Just the one. It's plenty.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Find a nice flat button to work on. That's your table.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: If it's got four holes, you've got four places to put things down, and one of them can be for your juice.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Now for the glue. We use honey. One drop. Only one!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: If you use two drops, you become part of the craft, and that's how I lost most of last Thursday.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Time for cutting! Never use the big people's scissors. They're the size of a bridge. Ask a ladybird instead. Ladybirds have very neat edges. Dot?

lines.speaker: Dot, the Ladybird
lines.text: Snip!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Thank you, Dot!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Made a mistake? That's all right! Blow on it, gently.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: At our size, everything blows away if you ask it nicely. Even mistakes.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Now we wait for it to dry. While we wait, let's look around. What's that big shiny thing?

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: It's a spoon! Hello, spoon! Look, there's your face in it! Upside down! Isn't that silly?

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Hold it up to the light! The light might be a lamp, or the sun, or the fridge door. Any of those is perfect.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Ooh. Look at it shine.

lines.speaker: Dot, the Ladybird
lines.text: Auntie Pim, mine's gone wrong.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Has it, Dot? Let's see.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Oh, Dot. That isn't wrong. That's a different thing. It's a lovely different thing. Let's call it a surprise.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: And there it is! Go and show a grown-up! You may need to stand on something and wave.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Well done, everybody! Pop it somewhere safe, where nobody can hoover it.

lines.speaker: Dot, the Ladybird
lines.text: Can I keep it, Auntie Pim?

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Of course you can, Dot. That's what crafts are for.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Song time! This one's about the hoover. Sing along, very quietly.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Here comes the hoover, hum, hum, hum.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Under the thimble, quick as a crumb.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Hold on to something, hold on tight.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: The hoover goes by, and we're all right!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Well done! Is everybody still here? Good.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Big shoes walking, one and two,

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: step to the side and let them through.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: They don't mean harm, they don't look down,

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: they're only big shoes, walking round.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Everybody knows this one! The Crumb Song!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: I found a crumb, a crumb, a crumb,

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: it's twice as big as my left thumb.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: I'll share it out with all my friends,

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: and that's the way the crumb song ends!

lines.speaker: Dot, the Ladybird
lines.text: Again!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: One raindrop, big as a ball,

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: rolled down the window and paid us a call.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: We said hello, and it said splash,

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: and off it went, in a silver flash.

clips.title: Auntie Pim's Safety Tip: The Hoover

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Auntie Pim's safety tip! If you hear a big hum getting nearer, that's the hoover.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Get under a chair, hold on to a rug tassel, and think heavy thoughts. Bricks. Mondays. Very full suitcases.

clips.title: Auntie Pim's Safety Tip: The Cat

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Auntie Pim's safety tip! If a cat looks at you, don't run. Cats love it when you run.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Stand very still, and look like a button. Cats aren't interested in buttons. Not for long, anyway.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Thank you to Ottilie, aged four days, for her drawing. It's a dot. It's a lovely dot. It's up on the fridge, which, for us, is a sort of mountain.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: And happy birthday to Benedict, who is six minutes old today! Well done, Benedict!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Halloween Crafty Corner! Today's costume is made from one sweet wrapper. Wrap it round you, and twist both ends. You're a sweet!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: Now, the big children will try to collect you. So roll away, as fast as you can. Happy Halloween!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: It's the Pumpkin Song!

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: The pumpkin's big, the pumpkin's round,

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: it's got a face, it's on the ground.

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: We'll climb inside and stay the night,

lines.speaker: Auntie Pim
lines.text: it's warm in there, and full of light.
